C-EXPORT-DOCUMENT-PIN.Summary: One exported artifact must come from one document: every export branch (styled HTML, Word, PDF, print) currently reads the live active tab at several await-separated stages — TOC and PlantUML fence counts before the consent cards, the styled render after them, the document directory and default file name after them again, and the disk write after the save dialog — with no identity pin, so a tab switch or an admitted external reload inside those user-time windows renders, embeds against or writes a different document than the one the user consented to export, silently. This change captures an immutable export pin — the document owner identity, the content revision and the pathname — at export entry, before the first consent card is raised; every later stage consumes only that pinned snapshot: identity is re-verified after each await that can observe a document change, the directory and default name are read from the pin and never re-read from the store; and before any byte is written the store re-verifies that the pinned document still owns the active surface and that the on-disk file has not changed since consent, refusing honestly with a localized notice instead of producing a silent mixture.
C-EXPORT-DOCUMENT-PIN.Problem: Confirmed against the current read-only state of the green-edit1 worktree (branch spec/export-document-pin, base 486275c7); source finding: the 2026-11-23 editor-zone scout record, complexity key F-003 ("export reads the document from the active tab at different stages"), re-verified line-by-line in this tree. editor.vue handleExport (:2382) is one async function spanning up to three user-time windows, and its reads straddle all of them. Styled HTML branch: flushSplit() (:2383), await getCssForOptions (:2390), getHtmlToc(editor.value.getTOC()) (:2391), countPlantUMLFences(editor.value.getMarkdown()) (:2403), await requestPlantUMLExportConsent — a sticky card that waits indefinitely for the user (:2402, gate block :2283-2380), editor.value.exportStyledHTML — a render of the live muya document (:2406), editorStore.currentFile.pathname — a fresh store read (:2420), await embedLocalImages with the requestScopeConsent card — a second indefinite user-time wait (:2423), editorStore.EXPORT({ type, content }) (:2435). The docx branch repeats the same shape (:2456, :2460, :2466, :2469, :2480). The store then reads currentFile again after all of it: EXPORT reads this.currentFile.filename for the default name (:2076) and awaits the save dialog (:2081-2087) before ipcFs.write (:2090); _EXPORT_DOCX reads this.currentFile.filename (:2114) and writes after its own dialog (:2134); _EXPORT_PDF awaits the save dialog before mt_export_pdf (:2155, :2163). A tab switch or an admitted external reload at any point inside these windows swaps the rendered muya document and this.currentFile together (the component re-imports the newly active tab into the same editor instance; the one reload-admission owner is util/externalReload, store/editor.js:2617), and nothing in the flow notices: the PlantUML fence count taken from document A rides as consent into exportStyledHTML rendering document B if the switch happens between :2403 and :2406; the embed pass resolves document A's relative image references against document B's directory if the switch happens between :2406 and :2420 — the scope-consent card then asks the user to approve B-dir paths for A's HTML; the default file name comes from whichever tab is active at :2076/:2114; and the final artifact is written from whatever mixture the stage order produced. The existing identity machinery guards other consumers but not export: renderedTabId/renderedDocumentOwner (editor.vue:540-541) gate rendering ownership and ext targeting (C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING, extBindingMatchesRendered :3389-3391), the link-check emit has its own seq guard (linkCheckSeq, editor.vue:3528-3544), and the save path has a full admission owner (util/documentSnapshot.js documentOwner :25-26; util/documentOperations.js sameOwner :25, sameVersion :27 and the invalid-save-acknowledgement refusal :71) — export alone reads time-separated live state with no identity check. The second gap is the disk: nothing verifies between consent and write that the on-disk file still matches the document the user approved exporting — an external modification that the buffer has not absorbed (reload declined or watcher absent) leaves the artifact describing consented content against a stale directory, with no honest signal. The consent gates C-EXPORT-BOUNDARIES shipped made the windows wider and user-paced (two sticky cards per styled/docx export), which is exactly what turns these stage gaps into user-reachable mixtures; pdf/print have narrower windows (no consent gates) but read the same unpinned live state before their dialogs (:2519-2531, :2552-2565).
C-EXPORT-DOCUMENT-PIN.Relationship: Builds directly on C-EXPORT-BOUNDARIES (applied): its two consent gates are the widest user-time windows this change pins, and their semantics are reused, not weakened — card copy, dedupKeys, the ten-locale editor.export consent keys and the decline behavior are untouched; the pin wraps around the gates so a decision is honored for exactly the document it was asked about, and an identity change after consent never re-runs a gate against another document silently — the export aborts with an honest notice instead. Same family, adjacent layers: C-EXPORT-SINGLE-PAGE (applied) and its successor C-EXPORT-SETTINGS-SECTION-RECOVERY (applied) own the entry points — one current appearance/page snapshot and stale-tab-callback protection at dispatch time (store/editor.js PRINT_DOCUMENT :2209-2214, EXPORT_DOCUMENT :2218-2220); this change pins the identity inside the flow, from the first consent raise to the write, which the entry-point guard never covered. The refusal-on-change semantics and the identity vocabulary are reused read-only from the save side: C-SAVE-CLOSE-DATA-SAFETY's util/documentSnapshot.js (createDocumentToken/documentOwner, :25-26) and util/documentOperations.js (sameVersion, invalid save acknowledgement, :27/:71) are the precedent the export pin mirrors — save admission already refuses a stale write, export never got the same contract. C-EXTERNAL-RELOAD-OPERATION (applied) keeps sole ownership of reload admission — untouched; the pin merely detects that an admitted replacement invalidated an in-flight export. C-MUYA-CURRENT-MODEL-EXPORT (applied) already guarantees muya's exportStyledHTML snapshots the current complete model at invocation (tests/renderer/muya/export-current-model.test.js); the defect is at the caller and store layers, so muya stays read-only. Neighbors in review, recorded for coordination: PR #321 (m045_ext — editor.vue EXT blocks, ~:3375+, disjoint regions from handleExport and the consent-gate block this change edits) and PR #325 (session — store/editor.js live-document/close zones, disjoint from the EXPORT/_EXPORT_DOCX/_EXPORT_PDF region); this specification is authored against the green-edit1 tree (base 486275c7), and the plan must rebase onto the actual delivery baseline, re-verify the two shared-file anchors there, and rerun both neighbors' regressions, per the C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY baseline-divergence precedent. Scout sibling bundles stay separate NonGoals: B (surface-ownership/close volumes, coordinates with #325), C (muya model surgery), D (focus/typography canon). Related debt recorded but not absorbed: the UNI F-007 remainder (export re-renders diagrams in a separate container and the raphael-marker global query in muya's exportHtml.js) and the linkCheck cross-file anchor gap (see NonGoals — both are different mechanisms, not document-identity work). Delivered through the repository technical-debt lane; lane departure into main and train accounting are separate owner-controlled steps.

Goals.Goal: Export document pin: at handleExport entry — after flushSplit and before the first consent card is raised — the flow captures one immutable pin for the active document: the document owner identity (tab id plus documentToken, the documentOwner precedent), the tab's content revision, and the pathname (null for untitled). The consent cards describe exactly that pinned document; the pin is never re-derived from live state during the run.

Stage guards consume only the pinned snapshot: after every await that can observe a document change (PlantUML consent resolution, exportStyledHTML return, embed pass return, save-dialog return) the branch verifies that the rendered document still matches the pin (rendered surface identity plus revision); the document directory and the default export name are read once from the pin instead of the currentFile re-reads (:2420, :2466, :2076, :2114). A mismatch aborts the export with exactly one honest, localized refusal notice — no artifact written, no partial dispatch, no gate re-run against another document; editing the document mid-export (revision moved) is refused the same way as a tab switch.

Pre-write identity and disk verification: store EXPORT, _EXPORT_DOCX and _EXPORT_PDF accept the additive optional pin and, after the save dialog resolves and before any write or print-to-file invocation, re-verify that the pinned document still owns the active surface and — when the pin carries a pathname — that the on-disk file has not changed since the pin was taken (the window.fileUtils.stat precedent; the plan pins one predicate: stat signature or content hash). A disk change is the same honest refusal naming the situation; cancel in the save dialog stays silent exactly as today (corner-2).

All four branches run the same pin contract: styledHtml and docx pin across their wide consent windows; pdf and print pin identity before their single render and verify before mt_export_pdf/mt_print_webview — they still never run either consent gate (C-EXPORT-BOUNDARIES corner C-12 unchanged). A pin-absent caller keeps today's behavior unchanged.

Honest surfaces and failing-first evidence: the touched module contracts, the M-011 graph summary, the touched file-local contracts and the V-M-011 verification entries state the pin contract; the named unit pins and the e2e artifact pin fail on pre-fix code and pass post-fix; the new refusal copy lands in all ten locales under the existing editor.export namespace.

Constraints.Constraint: Consent gates are not weakened: the requestScopeConsent and requestPlantUMLExportConsent cards keep their copy, dedupKeys, Confirm/Cancel semantics, count-only console markers and non-persisted decisions; the pin never suppresses, re-raises or re-targets a gate; pdf/print still never run either gate; declined PlantUML and declined embed references keep their shipped behavior for the pinned document.

Identity mechanism: the pin reuses the existing owners — documentOwner/createDocumentToken (util/documentSnapshot.js) plus the tab's contentRevision — and the disk check rides the existing stat surface (the runLinkCheck statFn precedent, editor.vue:3531-3540); documentSnapshot.js and documentOperations.js stay read-only; no new IPC command, no src-tauri change, no muya change (exportStyledHTML keeps its current-model snapshot semantics; every guard is caller-side or store-side).

Refusal voice: exactly one localized notice per refused export, under the existing editor.export namespace in all ten locales (de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW), following the C-62 all-locales pattern and gated by the locale-keys test; the notice names the situation class, never a path list beyond what the existing consent cards already show; console markers stay count-only (a BLOCK_EXPORT_PIN_MISMATCH class marker), keeping the V-M-065 privacy convention.

EXPORT signature is additive: the pin rides an optional parameter on the existing editorStore.EXPORT dispatch and its _EXPORT_DOCX/_EXPORT_PDF legs; the bus 'export' payload shape is unchanged; a pin-absent invocation (any current or future caller, other windows included) takes exactly today's path with today's re-reads — no caller outside editor.vue's four branches is required to change.

C-EXPORT-DOCUMENT-PIN.Assumptions: Plan-level requirements recorded from review: (1) the pre-write disk predicate pins a content hash (or stat plus hash) rather than a stat signature alone — a same-size same-mtime rewrite must not pass; (2) the residual window where content committed to the muya model but not yet synced into tab.markdown can render into the artifact without moving contentRevision is a known, named residual (flushSplit covers only the entry moment) — the plan documents it in the module contract rather than claiming it closed.

NonGoals.NonGoal: linkCheck cross-file anchor validation (linkCheck.js:168-174 — "file.md#slug" stripped to the file for existence, the slug never validated): not this bundle, decided by zone. The anchor's truth lives in another file's content on disk, not in the pinned active-document snapshot — validating it needs a new content-read scope over arbitrary target files (the read-scope/consent questions the C-EXPORT-BOUNDARIES family owns) plus the scout's fail-open behavior pin first, and in-document anchors already validate against the pinned document today (:152-163). Recorded as its own direction in the dead-link-validation zone; this change leaves linkCheck.js and dead-link-validation.spec.ts untouched and green.

The UNI F-007 remainder: export's separate-container diagram re-render (muya exportHtml.js) and the raphael-marker global query — render-isolation work, not document identity, partially closed by C-51 T-005; left for its own change.

No consent UI redesign, no remembered consent, no new export formats, no settings-page entries, no pdf/print consent gates, no change to what the pdf/print containers render beyond the identity guard.

No muya changes: exportStyledHTML/exportHtml snapshot semantics (C-MUYA-CURRENT-MODEL-EXPORT), the live preview, and the muya export surfaces stay untouched; no editor-zone surface-ownership rework (scout cluster B — coordinates with PR #325), no muya model-surgery work (cluster C), no focus/typography canon work (cluster D).
No preferences storage or schema changes, no save/autosave behavior changes, no changes to the reload-admission owner, no dependency acquisition, release version, tags or publication.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first e2e — "tab switch between consent and final write exports the consented document": a styledHtml document with a PlantUML fence starts exporting, the sticky consent card is left unanswered, the active tab is switched to a different document, then the card is confirmed — the identity guard refuses the export with the honest localized notice and mt_fs_write records nothing (the mismatch direction is the same refusal class as the disk-change sibling); today the run silently writes the new tab's document or a mixture, so the pre-fix red is pinned by asserting an mt_fs_write DID occur with the wrong-content signature — a state the fix removes. The sibling scenario — the file on disk changes after consent (shim stat flipped) — ends in the honest refusal notice with nothing written.

Failing-first component pins (editor-export-images.test.js harness): the pin is captured before the first consent raise; the directory handed to embedLocalImages comes from the pin, so a store currentFile mutation between consent and embed does not change it; an identity mismatch after consent aborts with the localized refusal and dispatches no EXPORT and runs no embed pass; a consent decision is never applied to a document other than the pinned one; the existing branch-wiring pins (call shapes, corner C-12 non-invocation, ten-locale consent keys) stay green.

Failing-first store pins (tests/renderer/store/export-document-pin.test.js): EXPORT with a pin whose document no longer owns the active surface or whose revision moved refuses before the save dialog and writes nothing; a pin whose pathname's disk file changed after consent (injected stat) refuses with the honest localized notice and writes nothing; a matching pin with an unchanged disk file writes exactly as today; a pin-absent EXPORT call takes the current path unchanged (compatibility callers), and cancel in the dialog stays silent (corner-2 preserved).

pdf/print uniformity pins: identity is verified before the single render and before the mt_export_pdf/mt_print_webview step; neither branch raises a consent gate; print-export, export-office and diagram-export e2e regressions stay green with no expectation drift.
Locale completeness: the new editor.export refusal keys exist in all ten locale files, the locale-keys suite passes, and no existing key is removed or reworded.

Graph and verification describe the final state: the M-011 SummaryDelta and the touched file-local contracts state the pin contract, the V-M-011 entry names the new evidence; all pre-existing export suites — the M-065 unit matrix, exportImages, export-docx families, muya export-current-model, export-html-images — pass without weakened assertions or budgets, and grace lint with --change C-EXPORT-DOCUMENT-PIN passes target and final assertions.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The named new tests pin the behaviors and fail on pre-fix code: consent-then-tab-switch exports the consented document (e2e artifact assertion at mt_fs_write), disk-change-after-consent refuses honestly with nothing written, pin-sourced directory survives a currentFile mutation, stale-identity EXPORT refuses before the dialog, matching pin writes as today, pin-absent callers keep today's path. The existing export families (M-065 matrix, editor wiring, docx dispatch, muya current-model, the four export e2e specs) are preserved as pre-change regression evidence, not relabeled. No Rust changes: no cargo command is required. Unavailable platform or owner acceptance evidence remains explicitly open and is not substituted by a shim.

Assumptions.Assumption: Identity is documentOwner (tab id plus documentToken) plus the tab's contentRevision plus the pathname — the vocabulary the save-admission owners already use; no savedAt-style timestamp exists on tabs today and none is introduced. The disk-change predicate (stat signature versus content hash) is a plan decision pinned once with rationale; the specification pins the honest-refusal contract, not the digest choice.

The pin is captured at handleExport entry, before the first consent card is raised, so every consent dialog describes exactly the pinned document; "the consent moment" in the goals means this first raise, and the pin makes it refer to one immutable document identity for the rest of the run.

Refusal copy wording per locale is plan and implementation detail; the specification pins key presence in the editor.export namespace, all-ten-locale coverage, the one-notice-per-refusal contract and the count-only console convention, not the translations.

The in-review neighbors (#321, #325) land before or after this change with disjoint regions intact; if the delivery order changes, the plan re-verifies the shared-file anchors on the actual baseline before pinning tests. Approval of this specification does not approve an unwritten plan, apply/archive, lane departure or release.
